Q: Why do nested flexbox items shrink differently? A:

The Firefox DevTools "Layout" tab explains the computations. Here's an example screenshot for one of the elements:

Let's read the first (blue) line of the "Layout" tab for each element, starting with the inner elements:

  • .a has width: 700px; and thus a "Base Width" of 700px
  • .b has some text, in my default font the "Content Size" is 160px
  • .inner contains the two things above, summing up to a "Content Size" of 860px
  • .c has flex-basis: 700px; and thus a "Base Size" [sic!] of 700px

Now let's traverse back from the outside to the inside:

  • .outer:

    • .outer contains .inner and .c, whose sizes have a ratio of 860:700, see above. Both have a flex-shrink value of 1 (see the second (pink) line of the "Layout" tab). So the numbers of pixels by which they shrink should have a ratio of (1·860):(1·700).
    • And their shrunk sizes should sum up to 500px because .outer has width: 500px; (near the bottom of the "Layout" tab, under "Box Model", it says 500).

    To achieve these two goals, .inner shrinks by 584.37px (see the second (pink) line of the "Layout" tab) to a "Final Size" (see the third (black) line) of 275.63px, and .c shrinks by 475.63px. I get a slightly different last digit with 860-500/(860+700)*860 no matter how I round, but whatever.

  • .inner's "Final Size" is 275.63px (see above). It contains .a and .b.

    • .b has flex-shrink: 1 (second (pink) line) but this is overridden by min-width: fit-content;, so it has the same "Minimum Size" (third (purple) line of the "Layout" tab) as its "Content Size" of 160px.
    • .a has flex-shrink: 1 (second (pink) line). For .b with 160px and .a to sum up to the 275.63px of their parent, .a shrinks to 115.63px.

Q: Why does the std module fail to compile with gcc? A:

GCC 15.0 supports it with -fsearch-include-path bits/std.cc.

g++ -std=c++20 -fmodules -fsearch-include-path bits/std.cc file.cpp

That will take a few seconds, once it’s done you'll have a cache file at gcm.cache/std.gcm. You’ll then be able to compile faster by removing -fsearch-include-path bits/std.cc from your command.

g++ -std=c++20 -fmodules file.cpp

References:

  • Commit adding std module
  • Commit adding -fsearch-include-path
  • Commit renaming -fmodules-ts to -fmodules

Q: In SAML, man in the middle attack, for unsigned saml response, can the attacker modify values? A:

Assertions can be signed separately from responses. I'm assuming you are asking about responses where the <Assertion> child tag is still signed, and only the <Response> parent tag is unsigned.

(Because if nothing is signed at all, then of course the attacker could modify anything.)

If my understanding is correct, an enveloped XML-DSig signature includes the entire parent tag by which it is enveloped. So an assertion signature signs not just the contents of the assertion, but also the whole <saml:Assertion> tag itself and its attributes.

Therefore the ID= attribute of the <saml:Assertion> is protected by the assertion signature (and so is the IssueInstant= and everything else), and if the attacker changed the assertion ID attribute (and adjusted signature reference accordingly) then the signature wouldn't match.

SimpleSAMLphp by default signs both the Assertion and the whole Response.

Q: Filter dict to contain only certain keys? A:

Using keyfilter from the cytoolz (or toolz) library:

from cytoolz import keyfilter

d = {"A": 1, "B": 2, "C": 3, "B": 4}
keyfilter({"A", "C"}.__contains__, d)

Result:

{'A': 1, 'C': 3}

keyfilter returns a new dictionary. To replace the exiting one, just assign back:

d = keyfilter({"A", "C"}.__contains__, d)

The first argument of keyfilter should be a function that takes a key and returns True if that key is to be kept, and False otherwise.

Here, I use as filter function the __contains__ method of the set containing the keys I'm interested in. Adapt according to your needs.

(cytoolz is supposed to be faster than toolz because it is implemented in Cython.)

Q: Is this a form of Black Hat SEO A:

When you created a php file and used file_get_contents, did you get this on your local machine? If so let me guess, you are with dodo internet provider?

This is not pulling data directly from that link that was sent to you. The website link was already taken down before you got to it and in turn was throwing a connection error. Looks like your ISP has literally shown you their own custom google search page.

Could be wrong but what you got is unrelated.
